Chapter 3. The Cost of Discipleship and the Call to Sacrifice.
There comes a moment for almost everyone on the journey of faith—a moment when following Jesus stops being just a nice idea and turns into something a little more real. Maybe it happens in a quiet conversation, during a late-night prayer, or even just crossing paths with someone who needs you. Suddenly, you feel those comfortable boundaries of faith start to stretch, and you find yourself asking, How much am I really willing to give up?
You might meet someone who’s already answered that question in a pretty radical way. Imagine a young couple who walked away from their promising careers and left behind the comfort of home to serve in a remote village. Their days are anything but easy—they’re learning a new language, living without modern conveniences, and facing all kinds of uncertainty. Yet, if you ask why they made such a drastic change, their answer is simple: They just wanted to follow Jesus wherever he led, no matter what it cost.
Hearing stories like that can be a little unsettling, can’t they? They force us to look at the gap between what we say we believe and how we actually live. Most of us want to follow Jesus—at least, up to a point. We’re happy to give, as long as it doesn’t mean real sacrifice. We’ll help out, as long as it fits into our schedule. But when we’re asked to give up our comfort, our security, or even our dreams, it’s easy to hold back.
The thing is, the teachings of Jesus don’t leave much room for half-hearted commitment. He called his followers to leave everything behind—to put him above family, above career, and even above their own lives. And he wasn’t just speaking in metaphors. For those early disciples, following Jesus meant giving up their homes, their possessions, and facing real persecution. Their faith wasn’t just a part of life—it was the center of everything.
Today, the cost of discipleship may look a little different, but the heart of it is still the same. Maybe it’s choosing a career that pays less because it lets you serve others. Or moving somewhere that’s less comfortable. It could even mean giving away resources you could’ve easily used for yourself. And sometimes, it’s about standing up for what’s right, even when it’s unpopular, or maybe even risky.
There’s one story that always sticks with me—a business owner who decided to use his company’s profits to help people in need. That meant taking a smaller salary, living more simply, and dealing with criticism from people who just didn’t get it. But over time, he found a purpose and fulfillment he’d never experienced before. The sacrifice wasn’t easy, but it brought a whole new sense of meaning to his life.
Most of us don’t realize just how tightly we hold on to comfort and security until we’re actually asked to let go. And honestly, it’s rarely a dramatic moment. More often, it’s a bunch of small choices—choosing to give instead of keeping, choosing to serve instead of being served, choosing to trust rather than trying to control everything. Little by little, these choices shape a life that starts to look a lot like what Jesus described.
So, I want to invite you to pause and think about what you might be holding onto. What would it look like to let go of some comfort and embrace the real cost of discipleship? The journey isn’t always easy. But if you’re willing to take that first step, you just might discover the fullness of faith you’ve been searching for.
